Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 344 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2024) 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) 344 is located within 
West-Central Alberta, covering an area of 3,602 km2. 
WMU 344 is bordered by William Switzer Provincial 
Park to the southwest, Highway 40 to the west, the 
Berland River to the north and the Athabasca River 
and Town of Hinton to the south. WMU 344 is 
predominately a forested unit characterized by high 
levels of forestry activity with an extensive network of 
all-weather roads. The habitat is largely coniferous 
forest; predominately lodgepole pine and spruce, with 
some mixed wood and deciduous stands. The 
objective of this survey was to update the population 
estimate and ratio for sex and age class of moose 
since the last survey in 2014. 
Survey Method 
An aerial survey for moose in WMU 344 was 
conducted February 27, 28 and March 1, 2024. 
Distance sampling methods (AEP 2016, Buckland et 
al., 2001) were used to determine moose population 
and density estimates. Transects (n=109), up to 10 km 
in length orientated east-west were established 
throughout the unit with 1.2 km spacing (Figure 1). 
Canopy over (0-33%, 43-66%, and >66%) within 10 
meters of the moose as well as activity (standing, 
bedded, moving) were recorded for each moose 
observation to include as covariates for the detection 
functions. Moose were classified by age, sex, and 
antler class. 
 
Results 
The total survey effort included 940.96 km of 
transects, and 25.2 hours of flight time. In total, 242 
moose were observed in 161 independent groups. A 
total of 224 moose were successfully classified, of 
which 99 were cows, 64 were calves, and 61 were 
bulls with 11 unclassified adults and 7 unclassified 
(age and sex). Only one (1) bull had antlers (small) 
due to the survey timing. Three sets of twins were 
observed.   
The bull:100cow:calf ratios were 66:100:64, with an 
estimated density of 0.62 moose/km2 (90% CI: 0.505-
0.749).  The estimated moose population for WMU 
344 is 2216 (90% CI 1818 – 2700) with a coefficient of 
variation of 12%. See Table 1 for a comparison to 
previous survey results. The moose population is 
estimated to have increased by 141% since 2014, 
representing an annal average population growth rate 
of 1.09 (90% CI 1.05 – 1.12). 
We also observed 106 white-tailed deer, 22 mule deer, 
and 243 elk (25 calves, 52 cows, 12 bulls, 4 
unclassified adults, 150 unclassified).
